name: Praseodymium
occurrence: Found alongside other lanthanides in monazite and bastnäsite ores.
majorUses: Welder's/glassblower's protective goggle glass (filters yellow light)
notableCharacteristics: Its name literally means 'green twin' in Greek, describing the pale green colour of its salts and its close relationship to neodymium (which it was separated from in 1885).
ncertRelevance: separation of didymium into praseodymium and neodymium
whyHere: Its three unpaired 4f electrons give praseodymium's compounds their characteristic pale green colour, a signature f-block trait tied directly to how those inner electrons absorb specific wavelengths of visible light.
didYouKnow: Praseodymium and neodymium were originally thought to be a single element called 'didymium' until 1885, when careful spectroscopy revealed it was actually two distinct elements hiding together.
genZNote: Used to be mistaken for its own twin element for years. Now it's out here filtering welders' goggles solo.
